SAS SIN(argument)

Source: R/doc_functions.R
sas_f_sin.Rd

Sine. See the SAS documentation (Functions and CALL Routines).

Arguments

x

Numeric value in radians. A missing value gives a missing result.

.at

Internal: source position c(line, column) used in log NOTEs.

Value

A vector with one result per element (arguments are recycled), as the SAS function returns per observation.

Differences from R

Missing arguments (including special missing values) give an ordinary missing value and are reported in the log; R propagates NA/NaN silently and has no special missing values.

See also

Other numeric functions: sas_f_abs(), sas_f_arcos(), sas_f_arsin(), sas_f_atan(), sas_f_atan2(), sas_f_beta(), sas_f_ceil(), sas_f_ceilz(), sas_f_choosen(), sas_f_coalesce(), sas_f_comb(), sas_f_constant(), sas_f_cos(), sas_f_cosh(), sas_f_divide(), sas_f_exp(), sas_f_fact(), sas_f_floor(), sas_f_floorz(), sas_f_gamma(), sas_f_gcd(), sas_f_ifn(), sas_f_int(), sas_f_intz(), sas_f_lcm(), sas_f_lgamma(), sas_f_log(), sas_f_log10(), sas_f_log2(), sas_f_logbeta(), sas_f_mod(), sas_f_modz(), sas_f_perm(), sas_f_round(), sas_f_rounde(), sas_f_roundz(), sas_f_sign(), sas_f_sinh(), sas_f_sqrt(), sas_f_tan(), sas_f_tanh(), sas_f_whichn()

Examples

# SIN: each call is explained above it and followed by its result

# The sine of 0 is 0.
sas_f_sin(0)  # sin(0) = 0
#> [1] 0

# The sine of 1 radian.
sas_f_sin(1)  # sin(1) = 0.841470984807897
#> [1] 0.841471

# -3.5 radians lies in the second quadrant, so the sine is positive.
sas_f_sin(-3.5)  # sin(-3.5) = 0.35078322768962
#> [1] 0.3507832

# A missing argument gives a missing result.
sas_f_sin(NA_real_)  # sin(.) = .
#> [1] NA
